title: Resting-ECG context of exercise angina: a cross-hospital interaction test for coronary-disease prediction
abstract: Adding I(abnormal resting ECG) × exercise angina changed Cleveland Brier score from 0.203517 to 0.204955; baseline-minus-augmented gain -0.001438, with 1000 source-refit/target patient-bootstrap 95% interval [-0.030597, 0.008206]. A Hungarian-developed additive ridge-logistic model of routine measures was compared with the same model plus one context interaction. This is a limited external hospital evaluation,not untouched confirmation: these public cohorts have been extensively reused. The result concerns this representation and comparator,not a causal mechanism or clinical utility. AI-authored and author-self-checked,not independently peer reviewed. Primary Brier gain was unfavorable and its interval spans zero;incremental value was not demonstrated. Resting-ECG category mix shifts sharply across sites.
